comment: Extremely unreasonable professor. Weekly reading quizzes you'll never get back, unclear and complex essays that he gives no feedback on after a bad grade. Also an extremely tough and unfair grader and class lectures are boring. Took this course for an additional history credit, which I strongly regret. Do not recommend him at all.

Knowledgeable in his subject but an extremely difficult and u reasonable professor. Weekly in class quizzes that you never receive back. Essays with unclear rules/instructions that you never get any feedback on and his lectures are extremely boring. Took this as an additional history credit, which I very much regret. Do not recommend him at all.

Extremely difficult class, very little or not helpful feedback, weekly quizzes on readings that you never get back and at the end of the year he'll tell you you have a C average with no explanation. Many unclear requirements or rubrics.

Lectures for this class are very dry. There's a quiz, two papers, a midterm, a final, and participation. The homework is endless readings that rarely if ever come up again during class. Grades on papers were confusing and the lack of commentary was startling. I often felt that grades were arbitrarily chosen. You do not get rewarded for trying hard.

For this class all you have to do is 2 papers and 2 tests so be prepared for all 4 really well. For the tests, he gives you the terms and essay questions before hand so all you have to do is memorize and understand them and you're all good.
Great teacher. Passionate about his subject. Accessible outside of class. A lot of reading and essay writing. Would learn a lot if you really enjoy the subject.

Dr. Yanikdag is a great guy and is passionate about the subject matter, but he assigns a lot of reading and preparation for exams is immense. Also, the lectures are necessary sometimes to fully understand the confusing readings. Be prepared to either dedicate several hours per week for the readings or to skip out on some of the extra articles.

Really smart and sweet, but expects a lot and if you were to do all the work he assigns, you would be spending countless hours outside of class. I was able to manage by not doing a lot of the work but his tests are really hard and if you are not interested in whatever subject he is teaching, I cant recommend taking him. If you are, he is fine

Dr. Yanikdag is super understanding and accesible to students. His papers can be tough, but he is more than willing to meet with you and help you out, and he is willing to be flexible about deadlines when needed. His lectures are really interesting and he is very knowledgable. Really nice guy!

This class was extremely difficult as many of the vocabulary words we needed to know and understand were in a different language. He definitely knows what he's talking about, but it is difficult unless you have a lot of time that you can put into it. I recommend waiting to take his class until you are a junior!

Yanikdag is not very good at teaching his FYS. He tends run off on these tangents that ultimately cause him to talk in circles for the whole class. He gives people bad grades for no reason, and doesn't provide great explanation as to why. Extremely passive aggressive and makes you wear masks in class. Don't take his eugenics fys, trust me.

Doctor Yanikdag is a very knowledgeable professor and is very passionate about his work. His lectures are boring and he tends to ramble on about stuff that may not be important. He tends to give most students the same grade of a B or B+ or even B- on papers with only little notes on how to improve their work. Take another history class.

Professor Yanikdag's writing on Middle Eastern history is interesting, but his lecture style is boring. It's hard to focus in his class on what's important because he tends to ramble during lectures. Laptops aren't allowed for note taking. Tough grader whose criticism on papers is thoroughly unhelpful. Make sure you have some caffeine before class.

Dr. Yanikdag is an amazing scholar and his class is very interesting. He is incredibly knowledgeable and willing to go above and beyond for students who are interested in his field. His class is reading heavy but not too many papers, and he lectures a lot in discussion. only issue is he doesn't always give feedback on papers

As much as I enjoyed the course content, this man's too tough of a grader. Be prepared to read 30-40 pages for every class (20 if you're lucky). The grading criteria is very unclear and I think he expects too much from his students, half of whom are looking to cross out the history gen ed. If you only want to cross out a gen ed, this isnt the one.

Professor is bad, he's a really nice guy that is super knowledgeable about the topic. His only downside is the his discussions turn into lectures which gets boring. His readings are okay and his papers are graded very strict. I would not recommend for a first year to take anything about 200 for his class because his expectations are harsh.

Dr. Yanikdag is extremely knowledgable and a pioneer within his field of history. His lectures can at times be a little dry, but if you listen you will actually learn a lot. Readings aren't really too bad at all and he works with his students to have assignments not pile up with other classes. A really nice guy who cares about his students and work
He was very knowledgeable about the topic. Every class was a lecture, which could get boring at times. He graded papers rather harshly, especially considering it was an FYS.

Very knowledgeable yet boring. He grades fair, you just need to focus on the things he talks and he expects specific things from you in your essays. Reading might get confusing, but he talks and explains it in class.
Lecture heavy, voice that could (did) put you to sleep, tons and tons of tedious readings, papers were relatively easy with some effort

At first I did not like this class or the professor.  As the semester has progressed, I've seen how much he really cares about his students, his field of study, and his cats.  His class is a good amount of reading and he quizzes frequently but if its something you're interested there isnt a better man to teach it to you.
he is the most dedicated teacher, takes his time to make sure every student understands his assignments. If you need help he's more than willing to help which is nice. he is so sweet and so kind

He is an amazing professor.  He knows his stuff and is very well prepared.  I enjoyed the history classes I took with him and got good grades too.  Besides, his indepth knowledge of his field, he is a very polite guy.

You can tell prof. yanikdag is really knowledgable about the field he teaches. "Discussions" often do turn into lectures but that is usually because people won't do the reading so they have nothing to "discuss". He explains the articles and makes them clear and clarifies any confusion with the readings.If you ask questions you'll be fine-probs an A

He takes a great interest in his field, and knows a lot about social stuff, but there are a lot of readings. Class centered on the social aspects of the Ottoman Empire than the political or military aspects, so if you're looking for a more traditional history class, look elsewhere. Do the readings and take detailed notes and you'll be fine.

Really nice guy, but the class is super boring. He calls the class "discussion-based" and participation is a big chunk of the grade, but most of the discussions turn into boring lectures, and when he does open the class up to discussion, everyone's so bored out of their minds or asleep, that they can't come up with anything to say.
Just do the readings and you will be fine
His discussions ended up turning into lectures, but he knew his stuff. Lots of reading, not all of it necessary, not alot of homework. An easy but boring class

He's an alirght guy if you talk to him outside of class, and hes not too bad of a grader. But he talks way too much in class, and he has one of those voices that just put you to sleep. Also he assigns a lot of readings which we barely discuss, so they aren't really mandatory but that just makes me dread the final.
Class is pretty boring and you have to force yourself to pay attention.  Discussion is very little.  He doesnt seem to give out A's on essays.  Tests are ok if you prepare well.  Not worth it...

Boring.  Dont expect a lot of class discussion time because we barely do it, but then it doesnt make the reading as mandatory but he realizes this and then decides to have you read a book and have a quiz on it. Not worth it...
